# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back (Lumbar) Fusion (CPT 22612)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-05, Reference Number POC-D89C6A76F0-15779**
**Member: Quinn Foster | Member ID: W310107367**
**Plan: HMSA (Hawaii Medical Service Association), Commercial/ACA, State of Hawaii**

To HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT code 22612. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking HMSA to reconsider its decision.

## Governing Policy

HMSA's stated reason for denial refers to the *2025 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines* (https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/2025%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines%20-%20HMSA%20FINAL%20eff%20070125.pdf).

## A note on the criteria cited

I want to be transparent with the reviewer: the specific policy language I have been given to reference in preparing this appeal is drawn from the sections of this guideline addressing **cervical fusion and cervical spine surgery** (neck-related criteria, such as ACDF and posterior cervical decompression). My procedure is a **lumbar** fusion, addressing my low back, not my neck. Because I do not have the lumbar-specific fusion criteria in front of me, I am not able to quote plan language that precisely matches my procedure, and I do not want to attribute cervical spine criteria to my lumbar surgery. I am asking HMSA to review this appeal against whatever section of its guidelines actually governs lumbar fusion (CPT 22612), and I am providing the full clinical picture below so that comparison can be made accurately.

## The Clinical Record

The following is drawn from my prior authorization packet and medical records:

- **Duration and nature of symptoms:** I have had 12 months of progressive low back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment completed:** I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 24 visits total, from 2026-05-14 through 2026-07-09, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-11, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings:** An MRI of my lumbar spine on 2026-05-28 showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Functional limitations:** I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf.
- **Exam findings:** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on my MRI.
- **Other relevant history:** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I would ask HMSA to look again at the MRI report described above, which documents a disc extrusion with severe stenosis and nerve root compression at L4-L5 — a finding that corresponds directly to my clinical symptoms (radicular pain into my right calf) and my exam findings (positive provocative testing and a matching neurologic deficit). My surgeon has reviewed this imaging together with my clinical history and has determined that surgery is medically necessary.

I have also completed a documented course of conservative treatment — physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and an injection — without lasting relief, prior to this surgery being requested.

## Request

I am asking HMSA to reconsider this denial in light of the full clinical record, including the MRI findings, the documented conservative treatment I completed, and my surgeon's determination that this procedure is necessary. If the guideline section that actually applies to lumbar fusion contains criteria not reflected above, I would welcome the opportunity to have my surgeon's office submit any additional documentation needed to address those specific criteria.

This appeal is being submitted within the time allowed. HMSA's notice states that an appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, by **2027-02-01**. I understand that submissions should be made in writing (unless expedited review applies), following the requirements in my Guide to Benefits, and that I should keep a copy for my records. I am sending this appeal:

- **By mail:** HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals, Appeals Coordinator, P.O. Box 1958, Honolulu, HI 96805-1958
- **By fax:** 808-952-7546 or 808-948-8206 (Oahu)

I understand that if this appeal is not resolved in my favor, I may have the right to request an external (IRO) review within 130 days, and that my denial letter is the authoritative source for that process.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Foster**
Member ID: W310107367
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
